Yahya Iranmanesh, Ph.D. Candidate
Instructor, Department of Computer Engineering Islamic Azad University, North Tehran Branch
Welcome
Welcome to my academic portfolio. I am a Ph.D. candidate in Computer Engineering (Computer Systems Architecture) and an instructor at Islamic Azad University. My research focuses on the design and implementation of novel hardware accelerators for neural networks, with particular emphasis on optimizing computational performance, minimizing power consumption, and enhancing scalability for complex artificial intelligence models.
My work bridges the gap between high-performance neural network algorithms and resource-constrained hardware platforms, enabling efficient deployment of AI-embedded systems across real-time applications including intelligent robotics, machine vision, industrial automation, and autonomous control systems.
Research Interests
Hardware Acceleration for Neural Networks FPGA-Based Prototyping and Implementation Neural Processing Unit (NPU) Design Embedded AI Systems Hardware-Software Co-Design Methodologies Machine Vision Systems VLSI Design and Digital Electronics Computer and System Architecture

Neural Processing Unit (NPU) Design#Custom NPU architectures optimized for specific neural network workloads, incorporating parallelization techniques and quantization strategies.
Hardware-Software Co-Design#Integrated design methodologies that consider both hardware constraints and software requirements to achieve optimal system-level performance.
Embedded AI Systems#Deployment of AI models on resource-constrained embedded devices for real-time applications in robotics, machine vision, and industrial automation.

content:
Yahya Iranmanesh is an Instructor at Azad University and a Ph.D. candidate in Computer Engineering, specializing in Computer Systems Architecture. His doctoral research is centered on the design and development of advanced hardware accelerators for neural networks.
Research Overview#His research addresses fundamental challenges in deploying artificial intelligence on hardware platforms with limited computational resources. Specifically, he has:
Conducted advanced research in hardware-aware neural network optimization Designed novel hardware accelerators focusing on computational performance, power efficiency, and scalability Developed FPGA-based prototypes for neural network acceleration Designed custom Neural Processing Units (NPUs) Implemented AI models directly on embedded devices Explored parallelization techniques and quantization strategies for low-latency inference pipelines His research integrates AI model design with hardware-software co-design methodologies, ensuring that embedded systems achieve both efficiency and reliability in practical industrial and research environments.
Industrial Applications#In the industrial sector, Dr. Iranmanesh works on designing fully automated production lines and converting manual machines into automated systems for various companies. His applied research has led to implementations in:
Intelligent robotics Machine vision systems Industrial automation Autonomous control systems Software Development#Additionally, he develops and implements dedicated software for full office automation platforms across multiple organizations. These platforms are AI-driven and incorporate:
Intelligent process automation Digital assistant systems Customer relationship management tools Sales optimization and workflow efficiency systems By integrating machine learning and AI algorithms, these systems enable organizations to automate repetitive tasks, provide intelligent recommendations, and improve overall operational productivity and decision-making processes.
Explore My Work#To better organize my academic, research, and educational activities, my work is presented across two dedicated platforms.
🔬 Academic Portfolio#A dedicated space for my research, publications, patents, and academic background. This platform serves as the scientific hub of my work, where I document peer-reviewed research, technical contributions, and ongoing investigations in hardware acceleration and embedded AI.
Focus areas: Research papers · Patents · Academic CV · Scholarly collaborations
